title: Short Stirling R9329
cause_of_loss: Fired on by shore defences crossing the coast near Plymouth on return; crashed 8 miles inland at 03:25
memorial_details: Rectangular granite freestanding stone of remembrance. Lettering is carved in black.
inscription: STIRLING BOMBER OF/ 149 SQDN RAF/ CRASHED HERE WITH/ THE LOSS OF/ 7 AIRCREW ON THE/ 21ST AUGUST 1942/ CREW:/ (Names)/ WE WILL REMEMBER THEM

sources.title: Facebook post by Daran Walker (RAF Bomber Command Memorials group)

narrative: In the early hours of 21 August 1942 (03:25), Stirling R9329 (OJ-V) of 149 Squadron was returning to RAF Lakenheath from a gardening (minelaying) operation in the Gironde estuary when it went off course. Crossing the coast near Plymouth, the aircraft was fired on by shore defences and crashed 8 miles inland at Gibhill Wood, Cornwood, Devon. All seven crew were killed.
